member.name: P:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_DC.Init_Success
member.summary: Value is true if the device controller was successfully initialized. If true, you may begin controlling the device. If false, refer to LastStatus_Code and LastStatus_Message for further information about the failure to initialize. member.name: M:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_DC.Notification_Register(System.Object,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_TellMeWhenTrayArrives,System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.String@)
member.summary: Calling this method registers your request to have your callback delegate called when the TargetDevice and TargetTray you specify have the status you specify in the RequiredMotionStatus and RequiredAlignmentStatus parameters. Valid values for RequiredMotionStatus and RequiredAlignmentStatus are: +1=true, -1=false, 0=don't care. The return value is an identifier for your notification request, which although not required, can later be used to remove your notification request via a call to Notification_DeRegister(). If the return value is zero, the notification request could not be registered. Setting AutoDeRegister to true, deregisters your notification request automatically once it fires for the first time. Setting it to false, causes the notification to be reset and fired again on a subsequent triggering event. Setting TimeOut to a value greater than zero, results in a notification being sent if that many seconds have elapsed and your event has not fired naturally. Note that AutoDeRegister=false is currently not supported. Note that you have to be very careful with your use of RequiredMotionStatus and RequiredAlignmentStatus. They are evaluated in conjunction with each other. Also, if you just want to know when the device starts to move after you issue a move command, it could be that the tray you request is already in position, or that it is retrieved very fast, so if you set RequiredMotionStatus to +1 (true), you may not be notified if the tray is already in position by the time you register the notification request. Note that when the controller status indicates motion has stopped, there may be a slight delay before alignment is set to true. However, for most purposes, the operator should be able to begin their task if motion is false, regardless of the alignment status. Alignment status becomes critical when you have other automated machinery interacting with the device being controlled.

member.name: M:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_DC.Get_Device_Status(System.Collections.Generic.List{Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_DeviceStatusType}@,System.String@)
member.summary: Returns true to indicate the "by reference" list contains valid detailed status of the devices being controlled. A return value of false indicates status was not available. Note that the list is zero-based where the number of elements equals the number of enabled devices. You _must-not_ use your device's unit number as an index into the list, as unit numbers could be of "any" value and are not necessarily consecutive, contiguous, or starting at a certain value. Note that when the controller status indicates motion has stopped, there may be a slight delay before alignment is set to true. However, for most purposes, the operator should be able to begin their task if motion is false, regardless of the alignment status. Alignment status becomes critical when you have other automated machinery interacting with the device being controlled.

member.name: M:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_C2000.Init_Controller(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.String,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.Int32},System.Object,System.Threading.SendOrPostCallback,System.String@)
member.summary:
This method must be called first (and return successful) before you will be able to obtain any useful results from any of the other methods of the class. Calling this method submits a request for the initialization of communications with the machine controller. It returns prior to obtaining all of the results of initialization. A return value of true only indicates the request process was initiated. If the parameters to this call change (typically EnabledDeviceUnitNumbers), you do not need to create a new object, simply call the "Close_Controller()" method and then call this method again.
You must pass parity as "NONE","EVEN", "ODD".
SimulationMode=true allows you to pass all unit numbers, enabled or not, and interact with the class, without any communications taking place with the machine controller.
LogLevel allows you to set how much logging will take place. Valid values are from 0-8 where 0 is least and 8 is most. A value of 2 is recommended for production operators where no issues are present.
The EnabledDeviceUnitNumbers may be a list or an array of the device unit numbers connected to the controller you want to drive. Device unit numbers need not be consecutive, contiguous, sorted, or starting at any particular value. Include only unit numbers of those devices that are enabled, unless you have Simulation=true.
CallersObject must be passed in order to receive initialization callbacks and drive notifications, otherwise can be passed as null. CallersDelegateHandler is a SendOrPostCallback to your method for accepting initialization status updates. Your callback delegate (optional by passing null) will be called at various stages through the initialization process indicating the current percentage of completion. You may also call Init_PercentageComplete() at any time to get the current percentage of completion. Note that, if all goes well, the initialization process only takes one or two seconds. It is only when there are issues that initialization begins a retry cycle and this could extend the duration of the process.

member.name: P:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_C2000.Init_PercentageComplete
member.summary: This method gives the caller access to the percentage of completion of the task launched by Init_Controller(). Values returned are in the range of 0 to 100. When the percentage of completion hits 100, you should then check the value of Init_Success to determine the results of the initialization attempt.

member.name: M:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_C2000.Drive_Device(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Submits a request to the controller to drive a device. Returns prior to any communications taking place with the machine controller. A return value of true reflects success submitting the request, not success of the drive operation. To obtain the results of the drive operation, call Notification_Register() to register for a notification callback or call Get_Device_Status() to get immediate status. Facing, Depth, and Quantity may be passed as zeros as they are not strictly required for driving the device but do disply on the operator panel. Display text is up to 80 character of text that will display on the operator panel, four lines of 20 characters each.

member.name: M:Hart_DeviceControllers.Hart_C2000.Show_Text(System.Int32,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Submits a request to display text on the device's built-in display. Returns prior to any communications taking place with the device controller. A return value of true reflects success submitting the request, not success of the display operation. Currently, there is no status available for the success or failure of this operation. Status of the display command could be available with additional programming. Note that the text is limited to four lines of 20 characters each for a total of 80 characters. Each of the four text parameters will be padded or trimmed (as required) to 20 characters each and displayed on a separate line of the display. As long as the text you send is 20 characters, any formatting you have provided (centered for example), will not be lost. Do not send blanks in all four text parameters to blank the display. Instead use the Clear_Text() method.

member.summary: Submits a request to clear the device's built-in display. Returns prior to any communications taking place with the device controller. A return value of true reflects success submitting the request, not success of the display operation. Currently, there is no status available for the success or failure of this operation. Status of the display command could be available with additional programming.
